**com** (noun): 1. Abbreviation of committee. 2. Abbreviation of community. 3. Abbreviation of communication.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**after** (adverb): 1. Behind; later in time; following. 2. Subsequently to; following in time; later than. 3. Subsequently to and as a result of.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**post** (noun): 1. A long dowel or plank protruding from the ground; a fencepost; a lightpost. 2. A pole erected to mark a spot. 3. The stakes that mark the beginning or end of a horse race

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**channel** (noun): 1. The hollow bed of running waters; the bed of the sea or other body of water. 2. The natural or man-made deeper course through a reef, bar, bay, or any shallow body of water. 3. The navigable part of a river.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**get** (verb): 1. To obtain; to acquire. 2. To receive. 3. To have. See usage notes.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**follow** (verb): 1. To go after; to pursue; to move behind in the same path or direction, especially with the intent of catching. 2. To go or come after in a sequence. 3. To carry out (orders, instructions, etc.).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**access** (noun): 1. A way or means of approaching or entering; an entrance; a passage. 2. The act of approaching or entering; an advance. 3. The right or ability of approaching or entering; admittance; admission; accessibility.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**first** (adjective): 1. Preceding all others of a series or kind; the ordinal of one; earliest. 2. Most eminent or exalted; most excellent; chief; highest. 3. Of or belonging to a first family.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**twitter** (noun): 1. The sound of a succession of chirps as uttered by birds. 2. Unwanted flicker that occurs in interlaced displays when the image contains vertical detail that approaches the horizontal resolution of the video format. 3. A tremulous broken sound.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**radio** (noun): 1. The technology that allows for the transmission of sound or other signals by modulation of electromagnetic waves. 2. A device that can capture (receive) the signal sent over radio waves and render the modulated signal as sound. 3. Any audio playing device, such as the on-board entertainment system in a car, usually including a radio receiver as well as the capability to play audio from recorded media; see also car radio.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**this** (determiner): 1. The (thing) here . 2. Referring to oneself. 3. The known (thing) .

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**here** (adverb): 1. In, on, or at this place (a place perceived to be close to the speaker); compare there. 2. At this point or stage (in a process, argument, narration, etc.) 3. In this matter.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**against** (preposition): 1. In a contrary direction to. 2. In physical opposition to; in collision with. 3. In physical contact with, so as to abut or be supported by.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**new** (adjective): 1. Recently made, or created. 2. Of recent origin; having taken place recently. 3. Additional; recently discovered.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**said** (verb): 1. Mentioned earlier; aforesaid. 2. Mentioned earlier; aforesaid.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**country** (noun): 1. The territory of a nation; a sovereign state or a region once independent and still distinct in institutions, language, etc. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. A large area regarded as distinct from other areas, e.g. because it is inhabited by a specific group of people 3. A rural area, as opposed to a town or city; the countryside.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**one** (numeral): 1. The number represented by the Arabic numeral 1; the numerical value equal to that cardinal number. 2. The first positive number in the set of natural numbers. 3. The cardinality of the smallest nonempty set.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**two** (numeral): 1. A numerical value equal to 2; the number following one and preceding three. 2. Describing a set or group with two elements. 3. The digit/figure 2.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**football** (noun): 1. A sport played on foot in which teams attempt to get a ball into a goal or zone defended by the other team. 2. The ball used in any game called "football". 3. Association football, also called soccer: a game in which two teams each contend to get a round ball into the other team's goal primarily by kicking the ball.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**manager** (noun): 1. A person whose job is to manage something, such as a business, a restaurant, or a sports team. 2. The head coach. 3. An administrator, for a singer or group. (Can we add an example for this sense?)

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**next** (adjective): 1. Nearest in place or position, having nothing similar intervening; adjoining. 2. Most direct, or shortest or nearest in distance or time. 3. Nearest in order, succession, or rank; immediately following (or sometimes preceding) in order.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**three** (numeral): 1. A numerical value equal to 3; the number following two and preceding four. 2. Describing a set or group with three elements. 3. The digit/figure 3.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**world** (noun): 1. The subjective human experience, regarded collectively; human collective existence; existence in general; the reality we live in. 2. The subjective human experience, regarded individually. 3. A majority of people.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**boss** (noun): 1. One who is in charge of something. One who oversees and directs the work of others; a supervisor. 2. One who oversees and directs the work of others; a supervisor. 3. A person in charge of a business or company.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**month** (noun): 1. A period into which a year is divided, historically based on the phases of the moon. 2. A period of 30 days, 31 days, or some alternation thereof. 3. A woman's period; menstrual discharge.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**president** (noun): 1. The head of state of a republic, sometimes also the head of government as well, particularly the head of the executive branch of the federal government of the United States of America. 2. A person presiding over a corporation, usually an executive overseeing daily operations under a chief executive officer but sometimes a separate position held by a CEO. 3. A person presiding over a meeting.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**link** (noun): 1. A connection between places, people, events, things, or ideas. 2. One element of a chain or other connected series. 3. Abbreviation of hyperlink.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**say** (verb): 1. To pronounce. 2. To recite. 3. To tell, either verbally or in writing.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**year** (noun): 1. A period of time akin to the time taken for the Earth to undergo a full cycle of seasons. 2. The time taken for the Earth to return to the same position along the ecliptic, completing a full cycle of seasons; a tropical year or solar year. 3. The time taken for the Earth to orbit the Sun with respect to the fixed stars; a sidereal year.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**government** (noun): 1. The body with the power to make and/or enforce laws to control a country, land area, people or organization. 2. The relationship between a word and its dependents. 3. The state and its administration viewed as the ruling political power.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**show** (verb): 1. To display, convey or exhibit; to have something available for others to see; to direct attention to something. 2. To indicate; to convey facts that lead to a conclusion. 3. To guide or escort; to show the way.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**top** (noun): 1. The highest or uppermost part of something. 2. The part of something that is usually highest or uppermost. 3. The uppermost part of a page, picture, viewing screen, etc.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**while** (noun): 1. An uncertain duration of time, a period of time. 2. An uncertain long period of time 3. An uncertain short moment.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**years** (noun): A very long time.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**home** (noun): 1. One’s own dwelling place; the house or structure in which one lives; especially the house in which one lives with one's family; the habitual abode of one’s family. 2. The place (residence, settlement, country, etc.), where a person was born or raised; a childhood or parental home; the home of one’s parents or guardian. 3. The abiding place of the affections, especially of the domestic affections.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**including** (preposition): 1. Such as, among which; introducing one or more parts of the group or topic just mentioned. 2. Introducing a finite clause.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**make** (verb): 1. To create. To build, construct, produce, or originate. 2. To build, construct, produce, or originate. 3. To write or compose.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**people** (noun): 1. Persons forming or belonging to a particular group, such as a nation, class, ethnic group, country, family, etc. 2. A group of persons regarded as being servants, followers, companions or subjects of a ruler or leader. 3. One's colleagues or employees.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**between** (preposition): 1. In the position or interval that separates (two things), or intermediate in quantity or degree. (See Usage notes below.) 2. Done together or reciprocally. 3. Shared in confidence.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**club** (noun): 1. A heavy object, often a kind of stick, intended for use as a bludgeoning weapon or a plaything. An implement to hit the ball in certain ball games, such as golf. An item used during routines, the apparatus consisting of a set of two clubs. 2. An implement to hit the ball in certain ball games, such as golf. 3. An item used during routines, the apparatus consisting of a set of two clubs.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**during** (preposition): 1. For all of a given time interval; throughout; in; pending. 2. At any time or period within a given time interval or while a given event is ongoing.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**now** (adjective): 1. Present; current. 2. Fashionable; popular; up to date; current. 3. At the present time.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**set** (verb): 1. To put (something) down, to rest. 2. To attach or affix (something) to something else, or in or upon a certain place. 3. To put in a specified condition or state; to cause to be.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**time** (noun): 1. The inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events. 2. The feeling of the passage of events and their relative duration, as experienced by an individual. 3. A dimension of spacetime with the opposite metric signature to space dimensions; the fourth dimension.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**across** (preposition): 1. To, toward, or from the far side of (something that lies between two points of interest). 2. On the opposite side of (something that lies between two points of interest). 3. across from: on the opposite side, relative to something that lies between, from (a point of interest).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**days** (noun): 1. A particular time or period of vague extent. 2. During the day.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**following** (adjective): 1. Coming next, either in sequence or in time. 2. About to be specified. 3. Blowing in the direction of travel, as opposed to headwind; downwind.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**game** (noun): 1. A playful or competitive activity. A playful activity that may be unstructured; an amusement or pastime. 2. A playful activity that may be unstructured; an amusement or pastime. 3. An activity described by a set of rules, especially for the purpose of entertainment, often competitive or having an explicit goal.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**head** (noun): 1. The part of the body of an animal or human which contains the brain, mouth, and main sense organs. 2. To do with heads. Mental or emotional aptitude or skill. 3. Mental or emotional aptitude or skill.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**state** (noun): 1. A condition; a set of circumstances applying at any given time. 2. A complete description of a system, consisting of parameters that determine all properties of the system. 3. A mess; disorder; a bad condition or set of circumstances.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**watch** (noun): 1. A portable or wearable timepiece. 2. The act of guarding and observing someone or something. 3. A particular time period when guarding is kept.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**alleged** (verb): Asserted (or supposed), but not proved.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**plus** (preposition): 1. And; sum of the previous one and the following one. 2. With; having in addition. 3. And also; in addition; besides (which).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**win** (verb): 1. To conquer, defeat. 2. To reach some destination or object, despite difficulty or toil (now usually intransitive, with preposition or locative adverb). 3. To triumph or achieve victory in (a game, a war, etc.).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**before** (preposition): 1. Earlier than (in time). 2. In front of in space. 3. In the presence of.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**coach** (noun): 1. A wheeled vehicle, generally pulled by a horse. 2. A passenger car, either drawn by a locomotive or part of a multiple unit. 3. A trainer or instructor.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**death** (noun): 1. The cessation of life and all associated processes; the end of an organism's existence as an entity independent from its environment and its return to an inert, non-living state. 2. Execution (in the judicial sense). 3. The personification of death as a (usually male) hooded figure with a scythe; the Grim Reaper.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**down** (adverb): 1. From a higher position to a lower one; downwards. 2. To or towards what is considered the bottom of something, irrespective of whether this is presently physically lower. 3. At a lower or further place or position along a set path.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**last** (adjective): 1. Final, ultimate, coming after all others of its kind. 2. Most recent, latest, last so far. 3. Farthest of all from a given quality, character, or condition; most unlikely, or least preferable.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**made** (noun): A grub or maggot.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**received** (verb): Generally accepted as correct or true.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**second** (adjective): 1. Number-two; following after the first one with nothing between them. The ordinal number corresponding to the cardinal number two. 2. Next to the first in value, power, excellence, dignity, or rank; secondary; subordinate; inferior. 3. Being of the same kind as one that has preceded; another.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**today** (adverb): 1. On the current day or date. 2. In the current era; nowadays; these days. 3. On the day of a recurring cycle or event which is currently happening.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**former** (adjective): 1. Previous. 2. The first of aforementioned two items. 3. Someone who forms something; a maker; a creator or founder.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**gen** (noun): 1. Information. 2. Information about the location of a bird. 3. Fan fiction that does not specifically focus on romance or sex.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**several** (adjective): 1. Separate, distinct; particular. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. A number of different; various. 3. Separable, capable of being treated separately.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**team** (noun): 1. A set of draught animals, such as two horses in front of a carriage. 2. Any group of people involved in the same activity, especially sports or work. 3. A group of animals moving together, especially young ducks.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**twice** (adverb): 1. Two times. 2. Doubled in quantity, intensity, or degree.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**according** (verb): 1. Agreeing; in agreement or harmony; harmonious. 2. Accordingly; correspondingly. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller}

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**again** (adverb): 1. Another time: indicating a repeat of an action. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. Back (to a former place or state). 3. Over and above a factor of one.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**day** (noun): 1. The time when the Sun is above the horizon and it lights the sky. 2. A period of time equal or almost equal to a full day-night cycle, being 24 hours long. 3. The time taken for the Sun to seem to be in the same place in the sky twice; a solar day.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**end** (noun): 1. The terminal point of something in space or time. 2. Share of joint responsibility. 3. The cessation of an effort, activity, state, or motion.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**face** (noun): 1. The front part of the head of a human or other animal, featuring the eyes, nose, and mouth, and the surrounding area. 2. One's facial expression. 3. One's facial expression.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**five** (numeral): 1. A numerical value equal to 5; the number following four and preceding six. 2. Describing a group or set with five elements. 3. The digit/figure 5.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**future** (noun): 1. The time ahead; those moments yet to be experienced. 2. Something that will happen in moments yet to come. 3. Goodness in what is yet to come. Something to look forward to.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**health** (noun): 1. The state of being free from physical or psychological disease, illness, or malfunction; wellness. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. A state of well-being or balance, often physical but sometimes also mental and social; the overall level of function of an organism from the cellular (micro) level to the social (macro) level. 3. Physical condition.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**international** (adjective): 1. Of or having to do with more than one nation. Between or among nations. 2. Between or among nations. 3. Participated in by two or more nations.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**life** (noun): 1. The state of organisms preceding their death, characterized by biological processes such as metabolism and reproduction and distinguishing them from inanimate objects; the state of being alive and living. 2. The status possessed by any of a number of entities, including animals, plants, fungi, bacteria, and sometimes viruses, which have the properties of replication and metabolism. 3. The animating principle or force that keeps an inorganic thing or concept metaphorically alive (dynamic, relevant, etc) and makes it a "living document", "living constitution", etc.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**latest** (adjective): 1. Last, final. 2. Most recent. 3. At the latest.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**police** (noun): 1. A constituted body of officers representing the civil authority of government, empowered to maintain public order and safety, enforce the law, and prevent, detect, and investigate crime. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. A department of local (usually municipal) government responsible for general law enforcement. 3. A branch of the Home Office responsible for general law enforcement within a specific territory.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**side** (noun): 1. A bounding straight edge of a two-dimensional shape. 2. A flat surface of a three-dimensional object; a face. 3. One half (left or right, top or bottom, front or back, etc.) of something or someone.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**services** (noun): 1. That which is produced, then traded, bought or sold, then finally consumed and consists of an action or work. 2. A service station.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**take** (verb): 1. To get into one's hands, possession, or control, with or without force. 2. To seize or capture. 3. To catch or get possession of (fish or game).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**under** (preposition): 1. Beneath; below; at or to the bottom of, or the area covered or surmounted by. 2. Below the surface of. 3. From one side of to the other, passing beneath.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**work** (noun): 1. Employment. Labour, occupation, job. 2. Labour, occupation, job. 3. The place where one is employed.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**year-old** (adjective): 1. Of the age of one year. 2. Someone or something of the age of one year.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**back** (adjective): 1. At or near the rear. 2. Returned or restored to a previous place or condition. 3. Not current.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**capital** (noun): 1. Money and wealth: the means to acquire or produce goods and services, especially in a non-barter system. 2. Already-produced durable goods available for use as a factor of production, such as tools and bulldozers (equipment) and office buildings (structures). 3. The capitalist class; capital owners considered collectively as a politically influential group — commonly represented by wealthy individuals and private institutional investors.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**decision** (noun): 1. The act of deciding. 2. A choice or judgement. 3. Firmness of conviction.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**for** (conjunction): 1. Because. 2. Towards; in the direction of. 3. Leading towards in time or circumstance.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**group** (noun): 1. A number of things or persons being in some relation to one another. 2. A set with an associative binary operation, under which there exists an identity element, and such that each element has an inverse. 3. An effective divisor on a curve.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**match** (noun): 1. Any contest or trial of strength or skill, or to determine superiority. 2. A competitive sporting event such as a boxing meet, a baseball game, or a cricket match. 3. Equality of conditions in contest or competition.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**midfielder** (noun): A player who operates behind the attackers and in front of the defence.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**outage** (noun): 1. A temporary suspension of operation, especially of electrical power supply. 2. The amount of something lost in storage or transportation.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**play** (verb): 1. To act in a manner such that one has fun; to engage in activities expressly for the purpose of recreation or entertainment. 2. To toy or trifle; to act with levity or thoughtlessness; to be careless. 3. To perform in (a sport); to participate in (a game).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**strike** (verb): 1. To delete or cross out; to scratch or eliminate. 2. To have a sharp or sudden physical effect, as of a blow. To hit. 3. To hit.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**tech** (noun): 1. Technology. 2. Technology businesses or the technology industry, especially in the field of computing and the Internet. 3. Technician; technologist.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**arsenal** (noun): 1. A military establishment for the storing, development, manufacturing, testing, or repairing of arms, ammunition, and other war materiel; an armoury. 2. A stock of weapons, especially all the weapons that a nation possesses. 3. A store or supply of anything.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**become** (verb): 1. begin to be; turn into . .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. To come about; happen; come into being; arise. 3. To be appropriate for.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**building** (noun): 1. The act or process by which something is built; construction. 2. A closed structure with walls and a roof. 3. Synonym of Tits building.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**move** (verb): 1. To change place or posture; to go, in any manner, from one place or position to another. 2. To act; to take action; to begin to act 3. To change residence, for example from one house, town, or state, to another; to go and live at another place; similarly to change the location of another establishment such as a business. See also move out and move in.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**action** (noun): 1. The effort of performing or doing something. 2. Something done, often so as to accomplish a purpose. 3. A way of motion or functioning.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**due** (adjective): 1. Owed or owing. 2. Appropriate. 3. Scheduled; expected.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**music** (noun): 1. A series of sounds organized in time, usually employing some combination of harmony, melody, rhythm, tempo, timbre, sound design, lyrics, etc., often to convey a mood. 2. Any interesting or pleasing sounds. 3. An art form, created by organizing pitch, rhythm, and sounds made using musical instruments and/or singing.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**money** (noun): 1. A generally accepted means of exchange. 2. A currency maintained by a state or other entity which can guarantee its value (such as a monetary union). (Can we clean up this sense?) 3. The total value of liquid assets available for an individual or other economic unit, such as cash and bank deposits.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**media** (noun): 1. The middle layer of the wall of a blood vessel or lymph vessel which is composed of connective and muscular tissue. 2. A voiced stop consonant. 3. One of the major veins of the insect wing, between the radius and the cubitus.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**major** (adjective): 1. : Greater in dignity, rank, importance, significance, or interest. Greater in number, quantity, or extent. 2. Greater in dignity, rank, importance, significance, or interest. 3. Greater in number, quantity, or extent.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**national** (adjective): 1. Pertaining to a nation or country, especially as a whole; affecting, shared by, or existing throughout all of a nation; the state. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. Belonging to or characteristic of a specific nation or country, as opposed to others. 3. Nationalistic; patriotic.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**player** (noun): 1. One that plays. One who plays any game or sport. 2. One who plays any game or sport. 3. An actor in a dramatic play.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**peace** (noun): 1. A state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony. For instance, a state free from civil disturbance. 2. A feeling of tranquility, free from oppressive and unpleasant thoughts and emotions. 3. Death.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**part** (noun): 1. A portion; a component. A fraction of a whole. 2. A fraction of a whole. 3. A distinct element of something larger.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**public** (adjective): 1. Able to be known or seen by everyone; happening without concealment; open to general view. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. Open to all members of a community, as opposed to only a segment of it; especially, provided by national or local authorities and supported by money from taxes. 3.
